Who needs Apollonius Rhodius, Bryan, when you have Don Chaffey? His 1963 feature *Jason and the Argonauts* features ground-breaking stop-motion animationnby the brilliant Ray Harryhausen--bronze giants! army of skeleton warriors!--as well as some delightful eye-candy. Here's Hera (Honor Blackman) and Zeus (Niall MacGinnis) observing goings-on in Thessaly, in what appears to be the bottom of a marble fish-pond: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H652ByzdD9s (Hera later comes back as a talking figurehead, but I couldn't find any good clips of that.) Here's the meetcute of Jason (Todd Armstrong) and Medea (Nacy Kovack)--shipwrecked, and yet not a hair out of place!: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=40TSBMyfik8 Why, watching this as a child, on Saturday afternoon TV, might lead one to become a Classics major in college! *** Happy this morning, and not just because I have the day off.

Does "Argonautica" sound like a CGI-generated, contemporary, action hero adventure movie that's like the 5th in a recent franchise?  I almost came here and made a complete fool out of myself.  Because when you give me XMEN and XBOX and DORY and the Riddler and the rock band founded by three sisters, I'm assuming the absolute worst in pop culture focus.  I was gritting my teeth over the "Argonautica" clues and cursing the puzzle that had inflicted them on me.  So imagine my surprise when the two answers turned out to be MEDEA and HERA, well-known in classical myth.  Had the action-film appropriated these famous figures?  Or is "Argonautica" NOT a contemporary action-film?

And, as it turns out, it is not.  I just looked it up, thereby saving myself much embarrassment.  Whew.

So 1) the puzzle is better than I thought.  And 2) I obviously need to bone up on the classics.

Some other thoughts.  I never knew that the Rick line was an ADLIB.  I was sure it was scripted.  And I loved the clue for LIFE.  I tried to guess, with no crosses, what Einstein had compared riding a bike to.  And I was right!
